thread:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT P0 — elevated generation tail latency in us-east-1. Paging eng oncall @alex_chang. Incident ID INC-2026-034. Observed increased retries and higher p95/p99 for text-generation endpoints. Please ack.
alex_chang: ack — I'm on it.
alex_chang: quick triage notes: a small subset of the gpu pool is experiencing OOMs during long-context workloads. Hosts hitting OOM -> retries -> queueing at frontends. Autoscale didn't compensate due to concurrent spot evictions.
maria_garcia: can someone draft an initial public notice for the status page? I'll coordinate and push once we have legal ok.
sam_lee: tagging in metrics: embeddings and non-generation endpoints mostly fine. Streaming and long-gen endpoints show errors or long tails.
jess_r: legal here — avoid words like "data loss" or definitive SLA impact until we've confirmed. Use "service degradation" and "potentially increased latency".
maria_garcia: initial status page draft below — please review quickly.

"""
Status: Investigating
Impact: Some hosted text-generation requests in US-East may experience increased latency or intermittent errors. Embeddings and most other endpoints are unaffected.
Start time: 2026-03-17 14:30 UTC
Details: We are seeing a subset of GPU hosts experiencing OOM conditions during long-context generation. Our on-call team is investigating and applying mitigations, including routing traffic to fallback model variants and restarting affected hosts. We will provide updates as we have more information.
Affected regions: US-East (primarily us-east-1)
Customer guidance: If you rely on low-latency long-context generation, consider temporarily reducing sequence length or using the small-model fallback via the model parameter. No evidence of customer data loss at this time.

"""

ops_lead: small edits: add incident ID and ETA note; add that we're routing ~60% of traffic to fallback which should reduce p95.
alex_chang: mitigation plan (short): 1) drain and restart failing hosts, 2) enable routing to fallback model variants for affected pools, 3) temporarily increase autoscale headroom for the pool, 4) monitor for regressions. ETA 30-45m for measurable improvement.
maria_garcia: updated copy with edits — replacing the block now.

"""
Status: Investigating (INC-2026-034)
Impact: Some hosted text-generation requests in US-East may experience increased latency or intermittent errors. Embeddings and most other endpoints are unaffected.
Start time: 2026-03-17 14:30 UTC
Details: A subset of GPU hosts in us-east-1 are hitting OOMs under long-context workloads, causing retries and increased queueing. Our on-call team is restarting affected hosts and routing traffic to fallback model variants to reduce latency. We have temporarily increased autoscaler headroom for the impacted pool. We will provide periodic updates as mitigation progresses.
Current mitigation: ~60% of traffic is routed to fallback model variants; affected hosts are being drained and restarted.
Customer guidance: If you rely on low-latency long-context generation, consider temporarily reducing sequence length or switching to the fallback model. No evidence of customer data loss at this time.

"""

maria_garcia: can legal sign off quickly? @jess_r
legal_bot: reviewed — wording approved with minor grammar tweak. Replace "No evidence of customer data loss" -> "We are not seeing any indications of customer data loss." jess_r: approved.
sam_lee: quick Q: should we call out streaming specifically? it's intermittent. alex_chang: added in copy above implicitly but can call out streaming degraded if you want explicit.
maria_garcia: will publish once ops_lead gives final.
ops_lead: good to publish. Maria, can you click publish and then post the link here? Also add note for escalation to account teams for customers with enterprise SLAs.
maria_garcia: publishing in 30s. will post link.

oncall-bot: Status page update published: https://status.redwood.example/INC-2026-034 — Initial notice live. :loudspeaker:

(35 minutes later)
alex_chang: mitigation update: restarted 5/7 affected hosts, routing stable at ~70% fallback, observed p95 latency improvement ~35% vs peak, error rate trending down. Still monitoring for full recovery.
maria_garcia: posting periodic update draft.

"""
Update (35m after initial): Mitigation in progress. We have restarted the majority of affected hosts and continue to route traffic to fallback model variants. Latency and error rates are improving; we expect further improvement as remaining hosts restart and autoscaler headroom stabilizes. No indications of customer data loss.

Recommended action: Continue to monitor and consider using fallback model for long-context workloads until this incident is resolved.

"""

ops_lead: please notify account teams for SLA customers, and prepare an email template for affected customers.
alex_chang: will confirm recovery criteria: all hosts drained and restarted, error rate at baseline for 10 continuous minutes, autoscale headroom restored.
maria_garcia: draft resolved notice once criteria met; I'll queue for legal quick review.

(after recovery)
legal_bot: resolved wording approved.
maria_garcia: publishing resolved notice now.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-034 resolved. Resolved notice published: https://status.redwood.example/INC-2026-034/resolved. All metrics back to baseline. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
